title: How do two arcs make an eye with a compass?
description: An almond eye is drawn from an upper arc and a lower arc, using two guide lines to place the compass tips. The video finds the tip positions and the opening so that the eye is symmetrical. Keeko raises the doubt about putting the tip above the eye for the upper arc.
teaching_notes: One idea: an upper arc is drawn with the tip below it, a lower arc with the tip above it, both with one opening and equally far from the middle. Watch for the slip of putting the tip on the same side as the arc.

source: How do you draw these eyes with a compass? Each eye is an almond shape made of an upper curve and a lower curve meeting at two pointed corners, with a filled dark circle (pupil) in the middle. The two eyes sit side by side and are identical.
video_script.why: The child uses the arc idea of the person to draw two identical arcs, one with the tip below and one with the tip above.
video_script.substitution: An eye six centimetres wide, with tips four centimetres from the middle line and an opening of five centimetres.
video_script.anchor: An almond eye made of an upper arc and a lower arc, with a dark pupil
video_script.wrong_answer: put the tip above the eye
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko wants to put the tip above the eye for the upper arc. A tip above makes the arc bulge downward like a bowl, but the upper arc must bulge upward, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Both arcs use one opening, and the two tips sit equally far from the middle.

final_answer.value: open ended; both arcs have equal radius, the tips lie on the line through the middle of the eye, one on each side, equally far from the middle (for an eye 6 cm wide: tips 4 cm from the middle line, opening 5 cm)
final_answer.spoken: both arcs use one opening, and the two tips sit equally far from the middle; for an eye six centimetres wide the opening is five centimetres and each tip is four centimetres from the middle line

never_show: the finished eye before the answer
maths_rules: Each curve of the eye is an arc, a part of a circle.
The corners are on the middle line, 6 cm apart, so each is 6 / 2 = 3 cm from the centre of the eye.
Upper arc: tip 4 cm below the middle line, opening 5 cm; each corner is 5 cm from the tip (3-4-5 right triangle, checked with a ruler); the arc rises 5 - 4 = 1 cm above the middle line.
Lower arc: tip 4 cm above the middle line, the same opening 5 cm; the arc falls 1 cm below the middle line.
Same opening and equal distance from the middle give two identical arcs, so the eye is symmetrical and 1 + 1 = 2 cm tall.
Slip: a tip above the eye makes the arc bulge downward, not upward.
video_script.design: One idea: the upper arc has its tip below, the lower arc has its tip above, with one opening. Uses the arc idea of the person. Wrong idea: the tip goes on the same side as the arc. The eye stays all video.
